purpose: Evidence-graded registry of external agent-memory results. This is not a unified leaderboard. Scores remain scoped to their original benchmark revision, dataset split, answer model, judge, prompts, memory corpus, and budgets.

direct_comparison_requires: same source corpus and ingestion trajectory
same judge model, rubric, and prompt
same memory/query prompt and tool-call limits
same context-token accounting and answer context budget
same number of evaluation items and scoring rules
paired per-question outputs and uncertainty estimates
never_pool: retrieval-only results with end-to-end answer results
vendor self-reports with independent matched-harness runs
comparability_policy.broca_status: No Broca score is entered until the exact runner, commit, dataset digest, model, judge, budgets, and raw per-item outputs are recorded.
comparability_policy.same_harness_note: OmniMemEval cohort results use shared benchmark data/prompts, gpt-4.1-mini answer model, gpt-4o-mini judge, and one score pipeline, but the harness is maintained by MemTensor (maker of MemOS) and public-doc adapters may not be product-optimally tuned. Keep these same-harness results in a separate comparison class from vendor self-reports.

results.benchmark_revision: paper evaluation protocol
results.comparison_notes: QEMem is the direct evidence-set sufficiency comparator. Its score is tied to its shared-memory-store protocol and should not be compared directly with vendor LoCoMo scores that use different reader/judge configurations.

results.judge: Vendor-published evaluation; details on vendor research page
results.comparison_notes: A strong commercial reference. Not directly comparable with QEMem or a future Broca result until the answer/judge prompts, corpus, context and scoring are matched.

results.benchmark_revision: vendor-published 500-question evaluation
results.judge: Vendor-published evaluation; details on vendor research page
results.comparison_notes: Do not compare with LongMemEval-V2 Small/Medium results; those are a different benchmark revision.

results.judge: GPT-5; identified by a third-party methodology audit

results.answer_model: GPT-5; identified by a third-party methodology audit of the vendor's run artifacts
results.judge: GPT-5; identified by a third-party methodology audit
results.comparison_notes: Different configuration and revision from LongMemEval-V2. Do not compare with AgentRunbook-C LongMemEval-V2 rows.

results.benchmark_revision: Small and Medium
results.comparison_notes: LongMemEval-V2 is a separate protocol with Small/Medium variants and latency-adjusted frontier scoring. Preserve those dimensions; do not compare its percentages directly with original LongMemEval 500-question or LoCoMo scores.

results.benchmark_revision: 42-question / 40-question / 11-completed-question pilot
results.answer_model: Gemini Flash-Lite; same reader/judge family across evaluated systems
results.comparison_notes: The same reader/judge and harness reduce some confounders, but the sample is small and Graphiti did not finish the full run. These are diagnostics, not a stable vendor ranking or SOTA threshold.

results.benchmark_revision: 2026-09-23 public run; 419 turns and 120 probes
results.comparison_notes: This is a different workload and recall metric, not LongMemEval or LoCoMo answer accuracy. It is useful for adversarial restraint and retrieval diagnostics.

results.benchmark_revision: 10 symbolic scenarios
results.judge: Symbolic Datalog oracle plus answer evaluation
results.comparison_notes: This measures evolving derived-state acquisition/maintenance, not generic conversational QA. It motivates the Broca D01-D47 diagnostic families.

results.benchmark_revision: 64 TaskSpecs
results.comparison_notes: This evaluates whether remembered facts may legitimately govern a decision, not only whether they are factually correct or retrievable.

results.benchmark_revision: GroundLM 2026; 8,500 questions / 41,203 versioned evidence pieces; headline result on 1,500-question stratified subset
results.comparison_notes: Do not compare LifeEM directly with LongMemEval or LoCoMo answer accuracy. LifeEM credits action-appropriate WARN_STALE, EXPLAIN_CONFLICT and ABSTAIN outcomes in addition to correct answer actions. The 62.3% figure is the stratified 1,500-question headline; the full 8,500-question run is 61.1%. The result uses Qwen3-8B and full lifecycle metadata is the upper-bound regime; timestamp-only and text-only regimes are separate stress settings.

results.benchmark_revision: 470 answerable questions; 30 unanswerable questions separately included in attempt coverage
results.metric: strict recall-all@5 (all required source sessions in top 5)
results.comparison_notes: This evaluates BM25 retrieval component only, not the daemon, full runtime, memory compression, answer generation, lifecycle governance or abstention. Strict recall-all is not answer accuracy. The page states that all 30 unanswerable questions were included in coverage but abstention quality was not measured.

results.benchmark: Three multi-hop QA benchmarks and open-corpus pilots
results.benchmark_revision: Findings of EMNLP 2026
results.metric: verification-aware redundant retrieval reduction with exact-match preservation
results.answer_model: Search agent unchanged; both gold expected-hop claims and generated claims evaluated
results.judge: Claim-evidence coverage verification and exact match
results.comparison_notes: HALT stops based on cumulative evidence coverage for every expected hop claim rather than generator confidence, fixed stop positions or lexical overlap. The paper reports redundant-search reduction while largely preserving exact match, but this ledger does not invent an unreported percentage. This is a direct conceptual baseline for Broca proof-coverage stopping.

results.benchmark: Multi-hop QA / HotpotQA utility and budget evaluation
results.benchmark_revision: 2026-07-27; 2,000-example Qwen2.5-1.5B experiments
results.judge: Correctness delta with/without retrieval and budget-frontier evaluation
results.comparison_notes: The paper defines retrieval value as marginal correctness change from using retrieved evidence versus a no-retrieval answer. It emphasizes that nominal budgets are not realized budgets and that retrieval can help, be neutral or harm. The reported 40–100% is the range of splits where common triggers overshoot a nominal 50% target when any overshoot is counted, not an accuracy score.

results.benchmark: Production RAG system and factuality benchmarks
results.benchmark_revision: EMNLP 2026 Industry Track
results.metric: external retrieval call reduction with matched answer quality
results.answer_model: Confidence-calibrated LLM; one epoch fine-tuning over 3K knowledge-graph facts
results.judge: System's production RAG evaluation and factuality benchmarks
results.comparison_notes: CONFRAG uses confidence-guided retrieval and parallel early stopping. It is a useful industry efficiency comparator, but confidence gating alone is not lifecycle validity or proof coverage. Its retrieval reduction and latency figures belong to its own real RAG system; do not assume direct transfer to Broca.

results.benchmark_revision: NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track; 263 paired tasks / 42 executable environments
results.judge: Deterministic environment commit/withhold check plus response judge

secondary_metrics.task_design: near-identical paired cases with one small decisive difference

results.comparison_notes: AgentAbstain evaluates whether tool-using agents know when not to act, with pre-execution and runtime abstention triggers. Only successful abstention (tool withheld and user informed) is credited. This is a broader agent-action benchmark, not memory QA or LifeEM.

results.benchmark_revision: 2026; five-level L1-L5 evidence quality gradient
results.metric: over-answer rate under L5 conflicting evidence
results.answer_model: Seven LLMs from five model families; three prompting strategies
results.judge: Automatic evidence-sufficiency evaluation with 200-sample human validation
results.comparison_notes: This benchmark focuses on evidence sufficiency and answer-abstention calibration. The 65-91% range is over-answering under conflicting evidence for the evaluated models, not a single pooled accuracy score. Use it as a failure-mode comparator for Broca's conflict and abstention policy.

results.benchmark_revision: 60 held-out articles; 188 questions; 169 evidence-evaluable
results.metric: evidence Hit@10 with adaptive hybrid-retrieval routing
results.judge: Evidence Hit@10; paired paper-cluster bootstrap; answer assessments provisional/model-assisted and not independently human validated
results.comparison_notes: The policy routes 46/188 questions to hybrid retrieval (24.5%) and reports evidence Hit@10 of 78.70% versus 76.92% for always-keep; paper-cluster paired bootstrap intervals do not establish a reliable utility advantage. Answer-level comparisons with quantized Qwen3-4B were provisional/model-assisted and lacked independent human validation. This is a cautionary comparator, not proof of answer-quality improvement or a headline SOTA result.

results.benchmark_revision: Provider's complete BEAM splits; 100K/500K/1M/10M history buckets; 2,000 benchmark questions over 100 conversations overall
results.comparison_notes: Past.dev's published run reports complete provider splits and separate ability scores; its BEAM 10M bucket is 200 questions over 10 conversations. The same page notes that competitor figures come from separately published vendor runs, not one common harness, so answer models, judges and configurations differ. It reports GPT-5.6-Luna as both answer model and judge for its own run. The 28.17% 10M multi-session score is more diagnostic for Broca than the 85.03% aggregate. This is a vendor benchmark claim, not independently reproduced by Broca.

results.benchmark_revision: BEAM 1M and 10M history buckets; managed platform, top-200 retrieval budget
results.comparison_notes: Mem0 publishes 64.1% at 1M and 48.6% at 10M with its managed platform and top-200 retrieval budget. It is a scale reference, not a head-to-head result against past.dev or Broca; model/judge and deployment configurations differ.

results.benchmark_revision: 100K/500K/1M/10M vendor-reported full splits
results.comparison_notes: Honcho publishes BEAM values alongside its own LoCoMo/LongMemEval results. The methodology page reports Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite as deriver and Claude Haiku 4.5 as dreamer/dialectic. The figures are vendor results and are not directly comparable to other providers' independently run BEAM figures.

results.benchmark_revision: Published full BEAM splits; sizes reported at 100K/500K/1M/10M tokens
results.comparison_notes: Past.dev's BEAM result page attributes these numbers to Hindsight's published results and says all provider values were separately published full-split runs, not a common harness. Do not treat rank or difference as a controlled head-to-head. The 200-question sample is the 10M slice; smaller-history slices use different sample sizes.

results.benchmark_revision: Published full BEAM splits; 100K/1M/10M tokens; 500K not published
results.comparison_notes: Past.dev's BEAM page attributes these figures to Exabase M-1 and says the vendor figures were separately published full-split runs using different models, judges and configurations. This is not a common-harness result or a Broca baseline reproduced under an identical setup.

results.benchmark_revision: BEAM 100K/1M/10M tiers; 500K not run
results.comparison_notes: Mastra reports two-run means over the same memory for each tier: 83.3% at 100K, 80.6% at 1M and 66.4% at 10M. The 10M run average is 66.4% (67.2/65.5) with a reported ±5.8-point error bar, described as within noise of Exabase's 68.0%. This is not a same-answer-model comparison: Mastra answers with Claude Opus 5.5, while Exabase used Gemini 3 Flash; judge is Gemini 3 Flash and memory observer/reflector use Gemini 3.8 Flash. With Gemini 3.8 Flash as the answering model, Mastra reports 78.4/72.8/57.8 at 100K/1M/10M. Its own ability analysis reports 25% 10M multi-session reasoning versus 74% at 1M. Mastra's page says the only other public multi-session score it knew was 9.6%, which is not reconciled there with past.dev's previously published 28.17% result; treat cross-vendor 10M ability comparisons cautiously.

results.benchmark_revision: ACL 2026 paper protocol
results.judge: Paper-specific LLM judge; see paper evaluation
results.comparison_notes: APEX-MEM combines temporal entity-centric property graphs, append-only event history and multi-tool retrieval-time conflict resolution. The 88.88% result is a paper-reported answer accuracy, not directly comparable with vendor results or LongMemEval-S Recall@20.

results.benchmark_revision: ACL 2026 paper protocol
results.judge: Paper-specific LLM judge; see paper evaluation
results.comparison_notes: APEX-MEM paper-reported result. Keep separate from LongMemEval-S Recall@20 retrieval metrics and other LongMemEval revisions/configurations.

results.system: Best evaluated memory system (system name not specified in abstract)
results.benchmark_revision: May 2026 paper; multi-party, asker-conditioned conversations
results.comparison_notes: GroupMemBench tests multi-party dynamics, speaker-grounded belief tracking and audience-adapted language. Abstract reports the strongest evaluated system at 46.0% average and says simple BM25 matches or exceeds most agent memory systems. This exposes a gap beyond dyadic user-assistant chat; do not treat 46.0% as an all-industry universal ceiling.

results.benchmark_revision: May 2026 preprint; heterogeneous documents/emails plus evolving dialogue
results.comparison_notes: RHELM synchronizes evolving dialogues with heterogeneous external sources such as documents and emails, and maps questions to at least one of 27 memory characteristics. No single aggregate result is recorded here because the abstract emphasizes comparative weaknesses without a headline numeric score.

results.benchmark_revision: Findings ACL 2026; weeks-to-months user conversations
results.judge: Automated memory-grounding checks and human evaluation
results.comparison_notes: Memora explicitly penalizes the reuse of obsolete or invalidated memories. The paper reports frequent stale-memory reuse across four LLMs and six memory agents; no aggregate FAMA percentage is stated in the abstract. This is a critical comparator for lifecycle correctness.

results.benchmark_revision: ICML 2026; 206 trajectories, 2,478 QA pairs, 6 domains, 4 capabilities
results.judge: Expert-curated QA and rule-based QA, per benchmark
results.comparison_notes: AMA-Bench covers agent-environment trajectories (states, actions, observations and tool outputs), not just dialogue. AMA-Agent uses causality graphs and tool-augmented retrieval. The 57.22% and +11.16pp are benchmark-paper results, not comparable to conversational answer accuracy.

results.benchmark_revision: ICML 2026; interdependent multi-session Memory-Agent-Environment loops
results.judge: Human-crafted tasks with explicit interdependent subtasks

secondary_metrics.task_families_list: web navigation; preference-constrained planning; progressive information search; sequential formal reasoning

results.comparison_notes: The paper reports that agents near saturation on LoCoMo perform poorly in MemoryArena. It evaluates whether memory acquired in early tasks is distilled and used to guide later actions; abstract does not report a single comparable aggregate percentage.

results.benchmark_revision: ACL 2026; 2,029 sessions and 400 memory-dependent tool-use tasks
results.judge: Human evaluation for task memory-dependence; seven frameworks evaluated
results.comparison_notes: The 91.3% value is the share of tasks rated strongly memory-dependent, not system task success. The benchmark asks whether an agent chooses the right tool and grounds its parameters using long-term memory.

results.benchmark_revision: Findings EMNLP 2026; seven memory systems and three-examiner defect attribution
results.metric: encoding evidence recall after recall-first AgenticRAG probing
results.judge: Independent encoding, retrieval and generation examiners; separate answer evaluation
results.comparison_notes: 95.6% is oracle/encoding evidence recall after a read-only, recall-first probing method, not end-to-end answer accuracy. The key finding is operational: retrieval defects dominated encoding and generation defects in the default LoCoMo setup. This motivates independent stage-wise diagnosis rather than aggregate QA only.

results.benchmark_revision: Findings EMNLP 2026; held-out transfer with shared GPT-4o backbone
results.comparison_notes: APEX-EM stores procedural and episodic traces in a typed graph and retrieves via semantic search, structural operation-signature matching and graph traversal. Same-backbone comparison reduces model confounding; this is a coding-agent experience-memory result, not conversational recall.

results.benchmark_revision: ACL 2026; multi-session image+text conversational memory

secondary_metrics.dimension_names: memory extraction and test-time adaptation; memory reasoning; memory knowledge management

results.comparison_notes: Mem-Gallery tests multimodal information preserved and evolved across long conversational trajectories. It is a benchmark-scope reference; headline system scores are not copied without matched protocol verification.

results.benchmark_revision: EMNLP 2026; paper-specific S* evaluation variant

secondary_metrics.evidence_tokens: Fewer than compared baselines; exact count not stated in ACL abstract

results.comparison_notes: Temporal-semantic hierarchical memory graph using temporal intent, entity activation, event-referenced constraints and graph propagation. The ACL abstract reports 66.3% on LongMemEval S* and +18.6 percentage points over its strongest baseline. Do not compare directly with original LongMemEval, LongMemEval-V2, or other S* variants without matching split, answer model, judge and prompts.

results.benchmark_revision: Findings of EMNLP 2026; canonical-pool LLM-QA control and raw-native ingestion
results.judge: Benchmark-specific QA / governance and activation evaluation

secondary_metrics.tracks: canonical-pool QA control; raw-native memory ingestion

results.comparison_notes: A benchmark profile, not a system leaderboard score. Raw-native evaluation exposes lifecycle-update, scope-boundary, provenance-recovery, activation and restraint failures that canonical-pool QA may hide. Keep the two tracks separate.

results.benchmark_revision: EMNLP 2026; five domains

secondary_metrics.capabilities: dense-history reasoning; implicit relevance; distributed evidence synthesis; semantically similar distractor resistance

results.comparison_notes: A benchmark profile, not an aggregate system score. The paper finds conventional factual recall does not guarantee evidence utilization; retrieval alone may recover useful evidence while the system still fails to integrate it or reject plausible distractors.

results.benchmark_revision: Findings of EMNLP 2026; conversational query styles
results.judge: Paper-specific retrieval-recall and end-to-end response evaluation
results.comparison_notes: A benchmark profile, not an aggregate system score. Conversational framing exposes retrieval gaps missed by QA-style probing, especially for implicit and composed requests. Strong retrieval does not automatically translate to strong response quality.

replication_first: Reproduce QEMem's LoCoMo protocol with the exact answer model, judge, shared memory store and context budget before making accuracy claims.
Register Zep and Mem0 vendor-reported results as contextual ceilings only until their exact configurations are reproduced.
